purpose: Insert the Japanese response that should exist between passive awareness of the reinforced Eastern Fleet and the rejected historical SA No.1 surface commerce raid. This node changes planning/ISR/submarine priorities only unless a dated strike gate is met.
branch_inputs: Japan has high-confidence indication by mid-January that a British heavy group is moving east and by late January treats the group as arrived in Ceylon.

Oyodo plus four modern destroyers and additional submarines were already released westward as an observation/contact reserve; second major surface reinforcement remained blocked by Central-Pacific priority.
After the 3-Feb Branch carrier battle, first-line mobile-fleet scouting/screen assets and trained naval aircrew have increased opportunity cost.
SLEUTH itself is not a Japanese trigger because no fresh Japanese contact with that sortie was adjudicated.

historical_anchors.event: Eastern Fleet diary records two hostile armed reconnaissance aircraft near Ceylon; the diary considers Trincomalee reconnaissance possible but says faulty navigation apparently prevented it.
historical_anchors.branch_use: Supports an already-existing low-cost Japanese Ceylon surveillance impulse; does not prove target-quality port intelligence.

historical_anchors.event: Ryu Ichi-go demonstrated that 331 fighters and 705 land-attack bombers could be coordinated with Army air forces for a long-range strike after deliberate staging and preparation.
historical_anchors.branch_use: Establishes planning competence and precedent, not automatic feasibility of a Trincomalee strike.

historical_anchors.event: Historical Japanese strategy did not favor a serious naval/air diversion to Southeast Asia at the expense of the threatened Pacific position while Eastern Fleet offensive capability was judged limited.
historical_anchors.branch_use: Caps the scale of a rational anti-Eastern-Fleet response unless fresh intelligence shows an imminent carrier/battle-fleet attack.

actions: Maintain Ceylon/Bay reconnaissance tasking from Andaman/Sumatra network.
Keep submarine intelligence/attack emphasis on Ceylon approaches and Bay/Indian-Ocean lanes.
Retain Oyodo group as fresh-contact exploitation reserve rather than free-ranging raider.
Accept the historical hostile armed-reconnaissance incident as a bounded Japanese probe in Branch unless contradicted by a later unit-origin audit.
Failure to obtain useful Trincomalee port picture prevents immediate strike release.

retro_decision_timeline.candidate: Night/low-light long-range land-based naval-air attack on Trincomalee shipping/air facilities, preferably after submarine or repeat-air reconnaissance confirms high-value fleet concentration.
available_tools: 705 land-attack bomber element before eastward crisis redeployment
331 fighter element for local/staging support; escort to Ceylon is range-constrained and not assumed
major_fail_gates: No fresh target-quality Trincomalee fleet plot after 7-Feb probe.
A daylight escorted mass strike is not attractive at Ceylon range; fighter escort margin is poor and British warning/fighter defenses are material.
After 3-Feb the opportunity cost of trained naval aircrew is high.
retro_decision_timeline.note: The proposal may exist at staff level; no retroactive bombs/torpedoes or losses are created.

actions: Central-Pacific emergency progressively closes the discretionary 705/331 strike window.
Continue submarine patrol/ambush, reconnaissance and port-exit watching as the preferred nuisance/suppression method.
Do not infer reaction to SLEUTH because Japan did not obtain a fresh track.

preferred_operation_concept.descriptor: Ceylon surveillance and submarine-ambush suppression package
preferred_operation_concept.priority_1: Fresh reconnaissance of Trincomalee/Colombo approaches and departure lanes.
preferred_operation_concept.priority_2: Submarine picket/ambush on likely heavy-ship exit routes, with intelligence reporting valued as highly as torpedo opportunity.
preferred_operation_concept.priority_3: Land-based bomber strike only on a recent high-value fleet/airfield cue and only while west-area bomber readiness remains adequate.
preferred_operation_concept.surface_role: Oyodo group exploits a fresh favorable contact or protects ISR/logistics; it does not conduct blind commerce raiding or seek battle-line combat.

why_no_immediate_trincomalee_raid.motive: MODERATE: Eastern Fleet is strategically irritating and can constrain Bay/Andaman freedom, but is not yet conducting a sustained offensive against Sumatra/Malaya.
why_no_immediate_trincomalee_raid.capability: PARTIAL: long-range bombers and reconnaissance exist, but escort and target-acquisition quality are limiting.
why_no_immediate_trincomalee_raid.slack: DECLINING_FAST after 3-Feb and especially after HAILSTONE/CATCHPOLE.
why_no_immediate_trincomalee_raid.payoff: Potentially high only if Illustrious/capital ships are positively located in a vulnerable concentration; otherwise expected attrition dominates.

effects_on_existing_progress.SA_No1: No change: historical surface commerce raid remains cancelled.
effects_on_existing_progress.SLEUTH: No change: sortie remains undetected at weapon-quality level.
effects_on_existing_progress.submarine_activity: Interpret existing Ceylon/Indian-Ocean patrols partly as Eastern-Fleet suppression/intelligence effort, not only merchant interdiction.
effects_on_existing_progress.705_331_redeployment: No reversal solely for Eastern Fleet. A later fresh carrier/battlefleet threat could create a new retention gate before aircraft physically depart.

future_trigger.if: Fresh credible information shows Illustrious plus heavy ships moving east/northeast toward Andaman/Sumatra, or repeated RN sweeps begin to interfere with Japanese bases/shipping.
future_trigger.then: Reopen a NEW anti-fleet air/submarine operation decision using capability, command-release, slack, motive/payoff, information-quality and opportunity-cost gates.
future_trigger.do_not: Auto-revive SA No.1 or invent a carrier/surface sortie from historical chronology.
